---
title: "Register your analysis plan on OSF"
description: "How to preregister a surveyframe study on the Open Science Framework: write the pre-analysis plan, complete the remaining fields, and upload it with the .sframe file."
---

A preregistration fixes your plan before you see the data. surveyframe
writes most of it for you.

## 1. Write the plan

In SurveyStudio, open your study before loading any responses and export the
report, or in R:

```r
render_report(instrument, output_file = "plan.pdf", format = "pdf")
```

The document is titled "Pre-analysis plan". It names the instrument's hash,
and lists the study, the participant information, the questionnaire, the
scales, and each research question with its hypotheses, method and decision
rule.

## 2. Complete the remaining fields

The plan ends with **To complete before submission**: exclusion rules, the
stopping rule, primary and secondary outcomes, multiplicity and contingency
decisions. Write them into the study's Preregistration fields in SurveyStudio
(Survey settings, Study), so they are sealed in the file, or answer them in
the registration form.

## 3. Register

On [osf.io](https://osf.io), create a project, choose a registration
template, and upload the plan and the `.sframe` file. The file's hash in the
plan lets a reader check, at [surveyframe.org/verify](https://surveyframe.org/verify/),
that the questionnaire you analysed is the one you registered.

## After registering

Change nothing silently. A change to the questionnaire or the plan is an
amendment, recorded with its reason, and printed in the report.
